candidates.summary: the -max-pages backstop aborts the whole render instead of truncating, so every page already crawled is discarded
candidates.failure_scenario: A pull request whose selected realms expose more than 400 crawlable pages (render-argument paths are uncapped, so one blog-shaped realm supplies them) makes Run return `page cap 400 reached (queue still had N)`; main.render (main.go:134) returns that error before Crawler.Write, so no HTML, no index.html and no preview comment are written and the render job goes red. The author gets nothing instead of a truncated preview. The same tool truncates its other cap: plan.go:257 keeps 25 realms and comment.go:86 prints the warning '%d more affected realm(s) were not rendered (cap reached)', and main.go:271 logs this very error from the baseline crawl and carries on. README.md:118 calls the page cap a backstop.
candidates.verify_by: tests/b9-catalog-pagecap_test.go, TestArgPagesBlowThePageCapAndDiscardTheCrawl: httptest realm serving 50 in-scope pages, MaxPages=10; expect a truncated crawl, observe a fatal error with the 10 captured pages discarded
candidates.evidence: go1.25.9, go test -run TestArgPages -count=1 ./... : `Run error: page cap 10 reached (queue still had 43)` and `10 pages were crawled and are thrown away: main.render returns this error before Crawler.Write`

candidates.summary: render-argument pages (/r/x/y:p/...) carry no per-realm budget, so one realm's whole argument tree is captured
candidates.failure_scenario: inScope budgets only the `file=` query argument (wantFile, GnowebFileBudget=2) and lets every `:args` path through unmetered, so a selected realm that renders one path per item yields one captured page per item. gno.land/r/gnoland/blog is seeded for exactly that shape (plan.go:41, 'render arguments (:page paths)'). Measured on one realm: 50 argument pages captured against 2 per-file pages. README.md:108-116 enumerates every shape the crawl skips and does not name this one, leaving it to the -max-pages cap, which does not truncate but kills the render (crawl.go:126); the ADR's 8.8 MB per preview and its 1 GB Pages budget (adr:80-96) were measured without such a realm, so the site-size bound the design rests on is unproven on this axis.
candidates.verify_by: tests/b9-catalog-pagecap_test.go, TestArgPagesHaveNoBudget: one realm serving 50 `:p/postN` links and 10 `$source&file=` links, FileBudget=GnowebFileBudget; count each class in c.pages
candidates.evidence: go1.25.9: `captured: 50 arg pages, 2 per-file pages, 55 total`

candidates.summary: a failed /public/_chroma/style.css fetch is swallowed, so source pages ship unhighlighted with nobody told
candidates.failure_scenario: Write keeps the chroma stylesheet only on `err == nil && code == http.StatusOK` and has no else branch, while the sibling check three lines up (crawl.go:315) does print a warning when the asset rewrite found nothing. A gnodev that answers 404 or errors on that path leaves every `$source` page in the preview without syntax highlighting and leaves the job log silent, so the reviewer reads the missing highlighting as a regression the pull request caused.
candidates.verify_by: read crawl.go:314-322: the chroma `if` has no else and no Fprintln on the error path, unlike the `n == 0` warning at crawl.go:315

candidates.summary: TestURLToFile pins _dir and _root outputs for URLs the crawl can never produce
candidates.failure_scenario: urlToFile's `listing` branch (crawl.go:490) and its `_root` default fire only on a base ending in '/' or on '/' itself. Both call sites feed them clean bases: crawl.go:142 runs on a URL that passed seedSet or inScope, and inScope rejects every trailing-slash base (pinned by crawl_test.go:83) while Seeds stops the directory walk at two slashes (pinned by TestSeedsSkipSingleSegmentDirs); comment.go:175 passes urlOf(realm). So the two rows document dead branches as behaviour, and the next reader maintains them instead of deleting the `listing`/`_root` handling.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rn 'urlToFile(' misc/gnopreview/*.go for the call sites, then confirm no seed and no in-scope URL ends in '/'

dropped.settled_by: grep -n 'for .*range ' misc/gnopreview/*.go: every map in an output path goes through sortedKeys (crawl.go:100, plan.go:229, plan.go:274) or sort.Strings (links, crawl.go:461), and writePages iterates the c.order slice; the repro run captured f0.gno and f1.gno, the two lowest sorted links, on every invocation.
